content.comment_body: I inserted an SD card that was not formatted properly for my device (raspberry pi). Even after trying a new card and performing factory resets, I am still stuck with the same screen. Is there a more thorough firmware reload that could resolve this issue? [article_no] [version_no] ([company_name] only)
For [product_name] [version_no], make sure the SD card is formatted with FAT32. The maximum supported size for the SD card is 32 GB.

I have submitted a service request. The device works fine, but I am unable to access the web server. The issue is only with the web page not loading. I suspect that the configuration files related to the open source software were damaged when Debian attempted to launch from the SD card. I'm hoping that a firmware or software restore can fix this.

If you're only seeing OSS information, then the web server might not be enabled, or as previously mentioned, custom web servers may not work due to an incompatible or non-functioning SD card. Verify if the web server is enabled on your [product_name]. Also, check diagnostics to see if the inserted SD card is compatible with [product_name]. Hope this helps.

That's right! After performing a factory reset, the web server will be disabled. I'll check this tonight and hopefully resolve the issue. This just shows how missing basic setup steps can cause major problems.

It turns out it was a beginner mistake. The SD card was set up for a Raspberry Pi, which corrupted the web server configuration on the [product_name]. When the web page failed to load, I performed a factory reset and then forgot to re-enable the web server in the new setup. Everything is working now. Thanks everyone. Quick tip: When you see the Open Source Agreement on the web page, it means you must enable the page through the Comfort Soft tools.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced trouble accessing the web server on their [product_name] after using an SD card meant for another device, which caused configuration problems. The main issue is unclear feedback and lack of guidance when misconfiguration occurs, such as after a factory reset or with an incorrectly formatted card, leading to the display of open source license information instead of useful errors or hints. Recovery steps, like re-enabling the web server with software tools, are not obvious to users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] web server to work seamlessly after factory resets and SD card changes, and to receive clear feedback or error messages if any configuration steps are missed.
